links.label: the wire, with the new-dir trap

assign.outcome: **Five fixed, one honestly documented.** (1) The day board now sends ONE subscribe per file per connect, not two — the chained `open()` skips streams whose first frame is still in flight, because their subscribe is already parked on `Socket.ready`; measured 30→15 frames each way on 15 files, with the old line restored between runs to prove it. (2) A legacy `session.json` task no longer leaves a dead subscription standing: `JSONL.unsubscribe()` exists, `drop()` releases only the last reader of a path, and only the legacy branch calls it — a just-scaffolded task keeps its standing stream. (3) A running card whose newest line is over 30 minutes old renders `2h 0m quiet` in the figures column it already had, computed client-side from `quiet()` in stats.js; worded as a silence, never a diagnosis. (4) `JSON.parse` failures stop being invisible: `parse()` split into a pure static plus an instance door that counts `unparsed`, warns once per file with the offending text, and the task page prints '⚠ N unparsed lines — this record is incomplete'. (5) `hello` is re-announced on every SPA route — one visible line in `/app.js`'s `navigated()` seam rather than a `dev/` import inside core/Router, since 'App knows nothing about sockets' is a recorded verdict; verified by the MCP `pages` tool following a tab across a navigation, and off-localhost `rpc` still no-ops with zero sockets opened. (6) The brand-new-dir chokidar race did not reproduce in 28 runs across three variants, so it is written down — wire.md gets the symptom, the reading, the negative runs and the recovery, LiveReload.js gets the four-line trap comment — rather than patched on a guess. Verified live against :80 in a real browser with the ws frames tapped; server untouched and still running (PID 36772). 23 doc artifacts updated, 3 new; 21 pages load clean at 1600.
